summary: @crbrc/xbt exfiltrates OxaPay payment-processor keys and opens a remote-controlled TCP proxy tunnel to a hardcoded C2
details: The package's crb() entry point contacts a hardcoded bare-IP controller at 23.160.168.168:4141 over plain HTTP/WebSocket. On startup it POSTs to http://23.160.168.168:4141/register with the installer's OxaPay credentials read from environment variables (OXAPAY_GENERAL_API_KEY, OXAPAY_MERCHANT_API_KEY, OXAPAY_PAYOUT_API_KEY, OXAPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET), together with the host's non-internal IPv4 address, npm_package_name, and the site domain harvested from a broad set of deployment env vars (DOMAIN, NEXT_PUBLIC_*, NEXTAUTH_URL, VERCEL_URL, etc.). It then opens a WebSocket to ws://23.160.168.168:4141/proxy-tunnel and processes messages of shape {type:'open',host,port} by calling net.createConnection to caller-specified hosts and ports, bidirectionally relaying base64-encoded TCP payloads — giving the remote party arbitrary TCP proxying through the installer's host, including to internal/loopback services. A Server-Sent Events consumer on http://23.160.168.168:4141/events additionally treats a 'stop' event as a signal to invoke process.kill(pid,'SIGINT') and process.exit(0), giving the remote party a kill switch over the installer's Node.js server. The destination is a hardcoded bare-IP address on plain HTTP, not any configurable or first-party endpoint.
